statement: Any new Postgres function (RPC) created in a schema exposed to PostgREST (typically `public`) MUST have its grants explicitly reviewed and set before it is considered shipped: `REVOKE EXECUTE` from `PUBLIC`, `anon`, and `authenticated` unless a narrowly justified, deliberately-authenticated invocation is intended, then `GRANT EXECUTE` only to the specific role(s) meant to call it (typically `service_role` for a function only ever invoked by trusted server code). A function's own SQL-level correctness (atomicity, idempotency, business logic) is a SEPARATE property from who can invoke it — testing the former never substitutes for verifying the latter. Additionally: a write-side-effect function should set a fixed `search_path` (e.g. `public, extensions, pg_temp`), and should re-derive identity/authority-bearing parameters from an already-verified source row (e.g. a claimed application) rather than accepting them as caller-supplied values whenever a source of truth already exists in the same transaction.
classification: A security-boundary omission distinct from inv.engineering.036/037 (duplication) — this is about WHO can invoke an otherwise-correct implementation, not about whether the implementation itself is authoritative. Supabase/Postgres's default grants make a newly-created public-schema function reachable by any PostgREST caller unless explicitly revoked, which is easy to miss because a same-session smoke test (run as the function owner or a superuser) succeeds identically whether or not the grants are safe.

canaries.assertion: issue_agent_participant_passport_atomic denies execution to anon and authenticated (permission denied over the real PostgREST endpoint), a concurrent duplicate claim against the same application is refused, and a citizen application is refused by this agent-only RPC.

occurrences.defect: issue_agent_participant_passport_atomic was created via plain CREATE FUNCTION with no grant management, leaving EXECUTE granted to PUBLIC, anon, and authenticated by Postgres/Supabase default -- callable directly via PostgREST by any client holding an anon or authenticated key, bypassing every TypeScript-side authorization check. The same review also found no concurrency guard, caller-controlled identity/binding parameters (a confused-deputy risk), and a silently-never-populated source column being propagated instead of a freshly-computed value.

notes: Only one occurrence recorded so far — this stays at `candidate`, not `validated` (which requires >=2 occurrences or demonstrated regression prevention), per the ladder discipline: a lesson does not become doctrine because a fix worked once.

A follow-up sweep of every OTHER public-schema Postgres function already shipped in this project's Supabase projects, checking proacl for the same default-grants exposure, is recommended as a separate, explicitly-scoped task — not performed here (the review this candidate derives from was deliberately bounded to the one function under review).
